extractedBy: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), overnight run agentpack-batch12, extraction worker
notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/chipgroup.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/chipgroup.md at 622cd82 (“docs: publish 11 Coin fixes on jfs-components v0.1.78-a116616”, 17 October), the same files on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note was checked on 17 October 2026 on the build it calls the 16 October build (mirror v0.1.78-a116616, Biscuit's main at a116616), so items citing it carry 2026-10-17 and 0.1.78-a116616. The evidence has three sections, each cited with its own date and build: 6 October on 3795b4c (636f3f5 noted as changing neither ChipGroup nor ChipSelect), 13 October on c1fa197 (#199 fixed: accessibilityLabel gives the row role group and aria-label; chips shrink to the row and wrap their label; strings and numbers render as text; #273 key warning found) and 17 October on a116616 (#273 fixed). Later sections supersede earlier ones where they disagree, so these 6 October sentences are not used: “the row is a plain `div` with no role and no name, and none can be passed”; “strings and numbers are dropped silently”; “A chip wider than the parent (long label) overflows with no truncation.”; the “role, or label” in “No `items`, `value`, `onChange`, `active`, `disabled`, role, or label.”; the upstream mdx's “The row is not an accessibility group.”; and the #199 and #273 gaps (both fixed). Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-a116616 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (222 files, complete) changes no ChipGroup or ChipSelect file and no design-tokens or react-utils file; the installed ChipGroup.tsx and ChipSelect.tsx are byte-identical to the a116616 tag, ChipSelect.tsx is identical back to 3795b4c, and ChipGroup.tsx differs from c1fa197 only by the #273 key line (140). Every sentence used here was read against the installed source, not run, with token values through the package's own getVariableByName: the row is flexDirection row, flexWrap wrap, alignItems flex-start with gap chipGroup/gap 8 both ways (ChipGroup.tsx 104–112), so wrapped chips start on the left; it has no width, padding, scroll or truncation of its own; ChipSelect's line is chipSelect/lineHeight 32 with no vertical padding, so each row is 32 px; an Active chip adds the 16 px ic_close icon after a 4 px gap (chipSelect/icon/size 16, chipSelect/gap 4; ChipSelect.tsx 165–167), the 20 px the guide gives; the Idle background is rgb(245, 245, 245) (grey) and Active rgb(246, 243, 255) with a purple label; each element child is cloned with the group's modes under its own and maxWidth 100%, flexShrink 1, minWidth 0 and overflow hidden (20–25, 136–143), so a chip wider than the row shrinks and wraps its label (ChipSelect's Text has no line limit); strings and numbers render as one-line Text (122–131); accessibilityLabel, accessibilityRole, accessibilityHint, accessibilityState and testID reach the row, and the role defaults to group when accessibilityLabel is set (116–118, 147–153); there are no rest props, so role and aria-label passed directly can't reach it. Each ChipSelect is a TouchableOpacity with role button, its label as accessible name, accessibilityState selected and aria-pressed on the web (ChipSelect.tsx 142–156), its icon defaults to ic_calendar_week (74), and it sets ChipSelect State itself from active, after any modes passed in (84–89), so the group can't set it. No guide sentence used here is contradicted by dbe0e02, so the entry carries no human flag. Two guide sentences are incomplete but true and are quoted as they are: the Group anatomy note “it has no state, only an optional spoken name” (the row also takes accessibilityRole, accessibilityHint, accessibilityState and testID; none is a visual state), and the States description “Chip Group has no idle, active, or disabled state” (accessibilityState is only forwarded to the row). The 6 October evidence sentence on a row parent (“In a row parent or a horizontal ScrollView the group takes its content width and never wraps”) still holds on dbe0e02: the row has no width or flex of its own, and the chip constraints added at c1fa197 resolve against the group's own width; read from source, not measured on dbe0e02. ChipSelect has a published guide but no entry in this pack yet. Chip Group only makes sense with ChipSelect children, and the guide supplies them (its Chips helper renders ChipSelect with label, icon, active and onPress, and an applied chip's label becomes its value, chipgroup.guide.tsx lines 22–28), so the examples use ChipSelect the same way, as earlier entries do with IconCapsule and MoneyValue. Rules about each chip's own look and state belong to ChipSelect's entry once it exists; this entry records what the guide says about the group and the filters in it. avoidWhen: the guide's Don't “Use chips for one choice” names no other component, so that rule has no useInstead; the 6 October evidence records the unpublished upstream mdx (cf988472) pointing a single filter to a ChipSelect alone and a mutually exclusive choice to SegmentedControl, so those two rules rest on that evidence quote and carry useInstead ChipSelect and SegmentedControl (both package exports; neither has an entry in this pack). The mirror ships no mdx, so that record can't be read against dbe0e02; the published Storybook's ChipGroup docs page (checked 29 October) is still the generated one (collections and design tokens only). The entry does not repeat the mdx's FilterBar claim, which the evidence says the guide deliberately leaves out. Strength: “The group only keeps the chips spaced as they change width.” is contextual (it is about the filters' state: the group also passes its modes and names the row); “never wraps” is contextual (a row parent or a horizontal ScrollView). Anatomy required: only the Group is always drawn; children is optional (no chips gives an empty row), the gap shows only between two chips, and a wrapped chip only when one doesn't fit. Content good keeps the guide's filter names and applied values; bad keeps the long labels from the Don't “Write long labels”. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every group), no modes, no style (the guide's Host VStack with width 100% and the 390 and 370 px frames are docs frames). The first is Configuration's “Figma’s three filters”, as the guide renders it (label and icon only). The second is the guide's In context once the screen has applied Date and Payment methods (the guide's Do “Let filters combine” shows the same two applied): the row named “Transaction filters”, each chip's active and onPress owned by the screen, an applied chip showing its value as its label; the literal values and empty onPress stand for the screen's own state and picker. Left out of examples: Six filters (its last three chips share ic_filter), the Anatomy and Sizing specimens, the bare States cards, the Do & Don't specimens and the playground. Not recorded: style and testID (developer-only, per the evidence's classification; the building rules keep style off Coin components); Dark mode and #201 (Active looks Idle in Dark: dark mode belongs to the brand team, not counted as a Coin gap); Figma's hex values; the evidence's browser measurements beyond what the guide states. Gaps: the Sources note's Figma and package difference (the chips are slightly wider on the web than in Figma, so Figma's 370 px group can't hold its three chips on one row: see Sizing), and its note that the published Storybook predates the current stories: re-checked 29 October, the published index.json was last modified 17 October 2026 10:39 UTC, its ChipGroup stories still use ic_loader and ic_rupee_sign (neither is in the installed icon registry; ic_status_loading and ic_payments are), and the ChipSelect bundled with them has no aria-pressed. Sorting (batch 12, round 1): one cross-check run on this entry, no flags. Its notes, not flags: #201 (Active looks Idle in Dark) is left out of gaps on purpose (dark mode belongs to the brand team, not a Coin gap); /facts/gaps/0 (chips wider on the web than in Figma) is kept as a Figma and package difference, as Toggle's, Summary Tile's and CC Card's entries keep theirs, though the evidence doesn't list it under Coin gaps; /placementAdvice/5 reads the evidence's row-parent behaviour (content width, never wraps) as discouraged, an inference from the group's wrapping purpose that the evidence states as behaviour, not guidance; /avoidWhen/1 and /avoidWhen/2 rest on the unpublished upstream mdx, as their wording says. No trace-check flags remain.

examples.purpose: Figma's three filters, from the guide's Configuration: Date, Status and Payment methods, each ChipSelect with its own icon, in one wrapping row. The screen adds each chip's active and onPress, as the next example shows.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup>
  <ChipSelect label="Date" icon="ic_calendar_week" />
  <ChipSelect label="Status" icon="ic_status_loading" />
  <ChipSelect label="Payment methods" icon="ic_payments" />
</ChipGroup>
